$doc: Vyomi capability registry — EventBridge (+ EventBridge Scheduler). See s3.json for the contract.

eventbridge.bus.crud.title: Event buses (default + custom; create, describe, list, delete, tags)

eventbridge.rule.crud.title: Rules (create with event pattern, describe, list, delete, enable/disable, tags)

eventbridge.rule.targets.title: Targets (SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis)
limitations: Only SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions state machines and Kinesis data streams are actually invoked. Other target types (API destinations, ECS tasks, CodeBuild/CodePipeline, Batch, Systems Manager, ...) are accepted and stored by PutTargets like the real API, but PutEvents never delivers to them — there is no silent fake success, the delivery simply never happens.

eventbridge.events.put.title: PutEvents — pattern matching + fan-out to matching rules' targets

eventbridge.archives.title: Archives (capture a bus's events matching a pattern)
limitations: An archive filters the bus's most recent 500 events (a bounded in-memory log), not a true unlimited-retention store, so RetentionDays can only be enforced within that window — it cannot bring back events the 500-event cap already dropped.

eventbridge.replay.title: Replay — redeliver archived events to their original rule targets
limitations: Replay is synchronous (completes inside the StartReplay call, not asynchronously over minutes) and is bounded by the same 500-event archive window as eventbridge.archives.

eventbridge.scheduler.schedule.title: Scheduler: schedules (one-time at(), rate(), cron()) and schedule groups

eventbridge.scheduler.firing.title: Scheduler: target delivery (SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis) when a schedule's time arrives
limitations: Vyomi has no background timer. A schedule's firing is computed and delivered the next time any Scheduler API call is made after its due time (console navigation and the periodic list/describe calls it makes are usually enough) — it does not fire on the wall clock while nothing is polling.

eventbridge.metrics.title: CloudWatch metrics (Invocations, TriggeredRules, MatchedEvents, FailedInvocations; Scheduler attempts/errors)

eventbridge.pipes.crud.title: Pipes (create, describe, list, update, start/stop, delete) with SQS source -> target delivery
limitations: Only SQS queues are a delivering pipe source; Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, MSK, MQ sources are accepted and stored but never polled. Enrichment, source filter criteria and target input templates are stored and not applied - the raw message body is forwarded.

eventbridge.connections.title: Connections (API key / basic / OAuth credentials; create, describe, list, update, deauthorize, delete)

eventbridge.api-destinations.title: API destinations (HTTP endpoint + connection + method; usable as a rule target)
limitations: CRUD is real on both substrates. Offline delivers a real HTTP request to InvocationEndpoint with the connection's API-key/basic auth; OAuth client-credentials token exchange is not performed and InvocationRateLimitPerSecond is stored but not throttled. On Nano the browser sandbox cannot make an arbitrary outbound request, so delivery counts as a FailedInvocation.

eventbridge.global-endpoints.title: Global endpoints (failover routing config over two event buses)
limitations: Control plane is real (create, describe, list, update, delete with validation). Vyomi simulates one region so no Route 53 health check is evaluated and no failover/replication actually happens.

eventbridge.sandbox.title: Sandbox: TestEventPattern (match an event against a pattern)
